stand: Lebanon remains in humanitarian and economic crisis after hostilities escalated on 2 March 2026. A ceasefire followed a June 2026 US-brokered framework on Hezbollah disarmament and phased Israeli withdrawal; violations continue. The sole "pilot zone" withdrawal, from West Zawtar in July, has not been repeated two months on. UNIFIL's mandate ends 31 December; the EU favours extending it and will launch a Lebanese army training mission. Lebanon's health ministry says Israeli attacks have killed over 4,300 people since March. Humanitarian partners seek US$331.5 million for 1.4 million people in need.

claims.text: Israeli attacks in Lebanon have killed more than 4,300 people since 2 March 2026, according to Lebanon's Ministry of Public Health.
claims.by: Says: Lebanon's health ministry, cited by Reuters. Denies: —

claims.text: An estimated 1.4 million people are directly affected and need humanitarian assistance.
claims.by: Says: UN-coordinated revised 2026 Flash Appeal. Denies: —

claims.text: Humanitarian partners are seeking US$331.5 million to fund assistance between June and August 2026.
claims.by: Says: humanitarian partners, via revised 2026 Flash Appeal. Denies: —

claims.text: Of the 1.24 million people in acute food insecurity, 1.14 million are in Crisis (Phase 3) and 101,000 in Emergency (Phase 4).
claims.by: Says: IPC Acute Food Insecurity Projection Update (Apr-Aug 2026).

claims.text: The 2023-2024 conflict's US$14 billion cost comprised US$6.8 billion in physical damage and US$7.2 billion in economic losses.
claims.by: Says: World Bank 2025 Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment.

claims.text: Lebanon's real GDP contracted 7.1% in 2024, with a cumulative decline of nearly 40% since 2019.
claims.by: Says: World Bank, cited in 2026 MSNA ToR. Denies: —

claims.text: Hostilities intensified sharply on 2 March 2026 amid wider regional escalation, driving fresh displacement and infrastructure damage.
claims.by: Says: 2026 MSNA ToR, drawing on ACAPS analysis. Denies: —

claims.text: Displacement and movement restrictions have severely damaged livelihoods and the wider economy.
claims.by: Says: ACAPS. Denies: —

claims.text: Telecommunications services in Lebanon have stayed operational despite insecurity and access constraints in the south.
claims.by: Says: WFP-led Logistics & Telecommunications Cluster. Denies: —

claims.text: Protracted displacement toward Beirut, Mount Lebanon, Akkar, Baalbek-El Hermel and Syria is straining host communities.
claims.by: Says: ACAPS, cited in 2026 MSNA ToR. Denies: —

claims.text: South and El Nabatieh governorates were among the areas most impacted by the 2023-2024 conflict, followed by Mount Lebanon.
claims.by: Says: World Bank 2025 Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment.

claims.text: In Bent Jbeil, Marjaayoun, El Nabatieh and Sour, between 55% and 65% of the population is projected to face Crisis or worse food insecurity.
claims.by: Says: FAO. Denies: —

claims.text: Hezbollah received $200 million from Iran to help families displaced by the war with Israel.
claims.by: Says: two sources with direct knowledge of the transfer; a Hezbollah official says an amount has been secured. Denies: US State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott says the money 'is not there'.

claims.text: Hezbollah plans to pay an initial $3,000 to each of roughly 50,000 affected families, prioritising those whose villages are destroyed or inaccessible.
claims.by: Says: sources with direct knowledge of the funding transfer. Denies: —

claims.text: Iran transferred $1 billion to Hezbollah in the first ten months of 2025.
claims.by: Says: US Treasury Department. Denies: Iran has never acknowledged financing Hezbollah.

claims.text: Lebanon's Prime Minister Nawaf Salam says total reconstruction costs from the two wars since 2024 could exceed US$27 billion.
claims.by: Says: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam. Denies: —

claims.text: More than one million people were displaced following the March 2026 escalation, mainly from rural areas.
claims.by: Says: FAO. Denies: —

claims.text: More than 22% of Lebanon's agricultural land has reportedly been damaged, and about 50% of agricultural land in South and Nabatieh is inaccessible.
claims.by: Says: FAO. Denies: —

claims.text: The UN Security Council has set 31 December as the end date for UNIFIL's mandate in Lebanon.
claims.by: Says: UN Security Council. Denies: —

claims.text: Shelter closures, including the Lebanese University Faculty of Arts, and consolidation measures caused significant anxiety among displaced households in South Lebanon.
claims.by: Says: ReliefWeb Emergency Protection Monitoring Report. Denies: —

claims.text: In the Bekaa, most displaced households had already returned following the ceasefire, leaving only a residual caseload in collective shelters.
claims.by: Says: ReliefWeb Emergency Protection Monitoring Report. Denies: —

claims.text: Israel's "pilot zone" withdrawal plan has stalled: West Zawtar, the only completed withdrawal, remains the sole example two months on.
claims.by: Says: Reuters/Al-Monitor reporting from West Zawtar; West Zawtar mayor Abed Ezzedine. Denies: —

claims.text: Israel's military says the pilot zone process has stalled because the threat of Hezbollah's weapons has not been removed; drones and movement curbs protect troops.
claims.by: Says: Israeli military, responding to Reuters questions. Denies: —

claims.text: The pilot zone process is "the only viable path" to security for Lebanon and Israel, and Hezbollah's disarmament is integral to it.
claims.by: Says: US State Department spokesperson. Denies: —

claims.text: West Zawtar's pilot zone programme has not succeeded, mainly because electricity and running water remain largely unavailable.
claims.by: Says: West Zawtar mayor Abed Ezzedine. Denies: —

claims.text: The EU favours extending UNIFIL's mandate to avoid a security vacuum in south Lebanon.
claims.by: Says: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas. Denies: —

claims.text: The EU will soon launch a training and advisory mission for the Lebanese Armed Forces and Internal Security Forces, hoped to be ready by year-end.
claims.by: Says: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas. Denies: —

claims.text: Lebanon is counting on EU support to find an alternative formula for after UNIFIL's mandate ends.
claims.by: Says: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun's office. Denies: —

claims.text: UNIFIL now numbers some 7,500 personnel from nearly 50 countries and has been in place since 1978.
claims.by: Says: UNIFIL/UN data, cited by AFP. Denies: —

claims.text: Lebanon is the EU's third-largest beneficiary of its European Peace Facility fund.
claims.by: Says: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas. Denies: —

timeline.text: Hostilities intensify sharply amid broader regional escalation, triggering renewed displacement and infrastructure damage.
WFP-led Logistics & Telecommunications Cluster activated to support the humanitarian telecoms response.
2026 Multi-Sector Needs Assessment Terms of Reference (V2.0) cites OCHA's toll of 3,884 deaths and 11,856 injuries since 2 March.
UNIFIL reports small-arms fire at its position near Kfar Shouba on the Blue Line; no casualties, incident under investigation.
Reuters/Al-Monitor report finds no further pilot zones agreed since July; West Zawtar still without reliable power or water.
EU's Kaja Kallas visits Lebanon, backs extending UNIFIL's mandate and announces an EU army training mission.
Ceasefire takes hold; partial returns and temporary easing follow.
Israel and Lebanon conclude a US-sponsored framework on Hezbollah disarmament, phased Israeli withdrawal and Lebanese army deployment to pilot zones.
Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem says the group will soon help fund a project to house people displaced by the war.
